tells: 1. The laugh never builds: across 1.0 s only the white-blouse woman lifts a hand and the front-row man in pink turns his head; mouths stay closed, no torsos rock, and the back rows don't move at all. It reads as a listen loop, not a laugh (club-5-strip.png, whole frame, all six panels)
2. The wide and the held frame are almost identical: the same poses and head angles on nearly everyone. The room looks frozen between samples (club-1-wide.png vs club-6-held.png, front two rows)

3. The front row repeats one resting pose: forearms on the table, hands clasped by the candle, upright spine, for the green hoodie, purple top, blonde and white blouse alike (club-1-wide.png, centre and right tables; club-2-mid.png, right half)

4. The face close is a dead-eyed half-smirk with plastic skin. The gaze looks past camera with no focus, there is no squint or cheek lift, and the expression doesn't say she is reacting to a line (club-4-face.png, centre face)

5. The back rows stand as frontal, evenly spaced, motionless dark figures, like a mannequin grid, and the near-black DOF outline around the close-up subject's shoulder and collar gives a cut-out halo (club-1-wide.png, rows behind the tables; club-4-face.png, right shoulder edge)

1. The front row sits bolt upright with both hands on the knees or in the lap, in near-identical mannequin postures with no slouch, crossed legs or leaning on the armrests (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-6-held.png, front row centre)

2. The back half of the house is flat black cut-out silhouettes of uniform height with no movement or variation. It reads as a painted backdrop of cardboard people (theatre-1-wide.png, top 40% of frame)

3. The man in the cap on the far right drops his head into his chest during the laugh, so his face disappears. It reads as asleep or broken, not laughing (theatre-3-mid.png, bottom right; theatre-5-strip.png, t=12.8 and t=13.0, right)

4. The face close laughs with the mouth only: the jaw is open but the eyes and brows are neutral, with no squint and no cheek lift. The disconnect is visible at TV distance, and there's a dark halo where the DOF meets the jacket collar and shoulders (theatre-4-face.png, centre face and shoulder edges)

5. The second row floats with no visible seats and looks like it is standing, and the laugh onset is half the row opening their mouths within the same 0.2 s while the row behind stays still (theatre-1-wide.png, second row; theatre-5-strip.png, t=12.6 to t=12.8, front row)

1. Only two people really laugh: the green-top and dark-hoodie women turn to each other, but the yellow-shirt man, the denim jacket and the back rows hold the same pose and blank stare all through the onset (openmic-5-strip.png, all panels, left half)

2. The face close has a jagged, combed streak artefact in the hair at the back of the head, and a dark ringing outline down the jaw and neck where the DOF meets the background (openmic-4-face.png, right side of the head and the neck edge)

3. Dark DOF halos outline every foreground figure in the held frame, the yellow-shirt man's face is grainy and noisy, and the bodies look cut out and pasted onto the blur (openmic-6-held.png, left figure, and the edges of the centre and right figures)

4. The front row hunches forward with hands on the knees in nearly the same pose. The dark-hoodie woman's lower legs read as bright pink/red stumps, and the left-most woman's arm hangs stiffly (openmic-1-wide.png, front row, centre right and left edge)

5. The light is flat and muddy: one brown wash with no stage key on the faces or rim separating the rows. The back row merges into a murky band, and the stray green exit light reads as a bug (openmic-1-wide.png, middle band and green dot at top centre; openmic-3-mid.png, top left)
